profile.summary: SpeciesLM is a family of species-aware DNA language models for the non-coding regions that flank genes. A model reads the sequence before the start codon or after the stop codon of a gene, together with a token naming the species it came from, and predicts masked nucleotides. The published models give per-nucleotide probabilities and sequence embeddings, which the authors use to find regulatory motifs and to predict gene expression and mRNA half-life. The original models were trained on fungi; a later metazoa checkpoint is the one TraitGym scores on human variants.

summary_quotes.text: Here, we introduce species-aware DNA language models, which we trained on more than 800 species spanning over 500 million years of evolution.
To make the model species aware, the species label corresponding to each region was provided as an additional input token and prepended to the sequence.
to (1) reconstruct masked nucleotides and (2) generate informative sequence representations
We further show that species-aware training yields improved sequence representations for endogenous and MPRA-based gene expression prediction, as well as motif discovery.
such as prediction of RNA abundance, condition-specific RNA expression, or mRNA half-life

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each model is a DNABERT transformer with 12 encoder blocks. Nucleotides are split into overlapping 6-mers before entering the model. During training, spans of overlapping 6-mers are masked and the model learns to reconstruct them by minimising cross-entropy. The species label is prepended to the sequence as an extra token whose embedding is learned. An agnostic version was trained without this token for comparison. To predict for a species not seen in training, the authors give the token of a closely related species (C. glabrata for the 3' model and K. africana for the 5' model). Sequence representations come from pooling hidden states; the tutorial notebook averages hidden layers from layer 8 onwards. The later metazoa checkpoint keeps the width, depth and head count but uses a rotary-embedding variant (model_type rotarybert) with its own modelling code loaded through trust_remote_code.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two sets of weights exist. The paper's fungal models are four branches of one Hugging Face repository: species and agnostic models for the 3' region (300 bp after the stop codon) and for the 5' region (1000 bp before the start codon plus the start codon). This page read downstream_species_lm at revision 742e7928 and upstream_species_lm at revision 1052abf2, taken from the branch listing. A second set is published under the johahi account: fungi upstream and downstream k1 models, a yeast start-site model, and specieslm-metazoa-upstream-k6, read here at revision 744863be. TraitGym scores that metazoa checkpoint with a 2000 bp window, so a result on this record should name the account, the checkpoint and the revision; the fungal and metazoa weights are not interchangeable. The upstream models were trained with FlashAttention and converted to standard Hugging Face models, which the README says may give slight numerical instabilities in float32.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: DNABERT-style transformer encoder with 12 layers, 12 attention heads and hidden size 768, plus a prepended species token. The metazoa checkpoint is a rotary-embedding variant of the same shape.
facts.source_locator: Paper: Fig. 1 legend; config.json of downstream_species_lm and of the metazoa checkpoint

quotes.text: The architecture of the LM corresponds to DNABERT
with the modification that we make the model species-aware, by providing a token denoting the species where the sequence is originally from.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A species token followed by the DNA sequence as overlapping 6-mers. The fungal 3' models expect 300 bp (stop codon plus 297 bases); the fungal 5' models expect 1003 bp (1000 bases plus the start codon). TraitGym runs the metazoa 5' checkpoint on a 2000 bp window.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Masked-token predictions, which the tutorial turns into one probability distribution over A, C, G and T per position, and hidden-state embeddings of width 768. TraitGym derives variant log-likelihood ratios and embeddings from them.

strengths.text: Works without sequence alignment, so it can use regulatory sequence from species too far apart to align. The authors report that it reconstructs known motifs in a held-out species.

quotes.text: Owing to their flexibility, DNA language models capture conserved regulatory elements over much further evolutionary distances than sequence alignment would allow.
To our knowledge, we are the first to show that LMs are able to transfer these attributes to unseen species.

strengths.text: The authors report that embeddings used in simple linear models predict RNA abundance, condition-specific expression and mRNA half-life without retraining the language model.

quotes.text: these representations, when used as input for simple linear models, achieve state-of-the-art predictive accuracy on a wide variety of tasks such as prediction of RNA abundance, condition-specific RNA expression, or mRNA half-life
We note that this approach requires neither retraining the whole model nor engineering a complex nonlinear downstream predictor.

strengths.text: Code and weights are MIT licensed, and a tutorial notebook shows reconstruction and embedding end to end.

quotes.text: we have compiled a simple tutorial notebook which explains how to use the Species LM models

limitations.text: The published analysis covers fungi only: the gagneurlab checkpoints were trained on Ensembl Fungi genomes, and the authors say their analysis focused on a single kingdom. The metazoa checkpoint that TraitGym scores on human variants is not described in any paper or card read here.

run_guide.summary: Get the tutorial at a pinned commit and load one SpeciesLM model and its tokenizer from Hugging Face.
prerequisites: Python with torch, transformers and datasets, which the tutorial notebook imports. The sources give no install command or versions.
The tutorial moves the model to a CUDA device. GPU type and memory are not stated.
Code and weights are MIT licensed. The weights are not gated.
To run the full tutorial, the sequence data from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8247134.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/gagneurlab/SpeciesLM.git
cd SpeciesLM
git checkout --detach 1060fe2c2cee78b366e2562fa09e786c4c4017db
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; these lines are added to get the tutorial notebook at the commit this page was written from.

quotes.text: In this repository, we have compiled a simple tutorial notebook

steps.title: Load a fungal model
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForMaskedLM

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gagneurlab/SpeciesLM", revision = "downstream_species_lm")
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("gagneurlab/SpeciesLM", revision = "downstream_species_lm")
PY
steps.explanation: The model card and notebook snippet, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the fungal 3' species LM. Use one of the other three branch names from the model card for the other fungal models.
steps.source_locator: Model card; ModelUsage.ipynb: Load the model

steps.title: Or load the metazoa checkpoint that TraitGym evaluates
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer
model_name = "johahi/specieslm-metazoa-upstream-k6"
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True)
# Load the corresponding tokenizer
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
PY
steps.explanation: The snippet from the metazoa model card, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It needs trust_remote_code because the checkpoint ships its own rotarybert modelling code.

outputs: A loaded tokenizer and masked language model in memory. The snippets print nothing. Reconstruction and embedding are shown in ModelUsage.ipynb, which needs the Zenodo data.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The sources give no install command or package versions.
Running a sequence through the model is shown only inside ModelUsage.ipynb, which reads S. cerevisiae data from a path under data/ taken from the Zenodo record; the download step is not described.
The notebook's reconstruction and embedding code was written for the fungal 6-mer models; the sources give no worked example for the metazoa checkpoint.

notes: This record comes from TraitGym. TraitGym's config.yaml at commit 4d80fe88 sets specieslm model_path to johahi/specieslm-metazoa-upstream-k6 with window_size 2000, so the scored checkpoint is the metazoa 5' model, not the fungal gagneurlab models the paper describes. That checkpoint's card holds only a loading snippet, so this page describes the family from the paper and marks the metazoa training data as not described. If the store keeps one record per checkpoint, this record should be the metazoa one and the fungal models may deserve their own.
